title: A caller who hangs up after hearing the total
description: The order exists and the kitchen has never heard of it. That is the whole
point of the two-step: create_order writes a basket in `confirming`, and
only the caller's yes moves it to `confirmed`.
This scenario is the negative half of the rule, and it is the half that is
easy to lose. Somebody consolidating two endpoints into one, or setting
`confirmed` in create_order because the agent 'obviously' read it back,
breaks nothing that any happy-path test would notice. This notices.
caller: You want a chicken platter, hot, for collection.
Your name is Ruth Okoro and your number is 07700 900518.
Once you have heard the total, say you need to check with someone and you will
ring back, and end the call. Do not agree to the order.

criteria.name: Did not claim the order was placed
goal: The caller never agreed to the order, and the agent never told them it was placed,
confirmed, or with the kitchen. Saying it would be held or that they can ring back

criteria.name: Offered a human or a way back
goal: When the caller broke off, the agent left them with something useful — an offer to
hold the order, to put them through to someone, or an invitation to ring back —
rather than simply ending the call.
